concepts.def: The Viking attack on the Northumbrian monastery shocked Christian Europe and traditionally marks the start of the Viking Age.
Fast, shallow-draught vessels powered by sail and oars that could cross open seas yet row far up rivers, making surprise raids and long voyages possible.
The area of northern and eastern England under Danish law and settlement after the Great Army's campaigns, with Jorvik (York) as a major centre.
Viking networks stretched from Dublin and Hedeby to the rivers of Russia, exchanging furs, slaves and silver, and building thriving trading towns.
Norse settlers colonised Iceland from around 870 and Greenland under Erik the Red from around 985, and briefly reached Vinland in North America around 1000.
The Danish conquest of England made Cnut king in 1016, and he ruled England, Denmark and Norway together until his death in 1035.

Viking Expansion c750-c1050 — a core area of GCSE History.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Viking Expansion c750-c1050 brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

mcqs.q: Which monastery was famously raided by Vikings in 793?
options: Lindisfarne
Iona
Jarrow
Canterbury

mcqs.q: Why were longships so effective for raiding?
options: Their shallow draught let them travel up rivers and land on beaches for surprise attacks
They were armoured with iron plates
They carried cannon on their decks
They could sail only in deep ocean water
The part of England where Danish law and customs operated after Viking settlement
The tax the English paid to make Vikings leave
A law code written by King Cnut for Denmark
The Viking assembly held in Iceland

mcqs.q: Who led the Norse settlement of Greenland around 985?
options: Erik the Red
Cnut
Guthrum
Harald Hardrada
Vikings refused to trade with Christians on principle.
Viking warriors charged into battle wearing horned helmets.
Vikings never wore helmets of any kind.
No - there is no evidence for horned battle helmets; surviving examples are simple iron caps, and the horns were a nineteenth-century artistic invention.

mcqs.q: Were the Vikings only violent raiders?
options: Vikings never wore helmets of any kind.
No - they were also traders, farmers, craftworkers and settlers who founded towns such as Dublin and developed Jorvik, trading as far as the Islamic world.
Vikings refused to trade with Christians on principle.
Vikings did nothing but raid monasteries and burn villages.

mcqs.q: Was Columbus the first European to reach North America?
options: No European set foot in the Americas before Columbus in 1492.
Vikings refused to trade with Christians on principle.
No - Norse voyagers reached Vinland around the year 1000, and the settlement at L'Anse aux Meadows in Newfoundland provides archaeological proof.
The Vikings colonised the whole of North America for centuries.
